Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Uganda has general data protection legislation: the Data Protection and Privacy Act (includes privacy protection for customer information) complemented by payment-sector confidentiality/privacy provisions in the National Payment Systems Act (e.g., protection of customer information).
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched and confirmed relevant. The DLA Piper page confirms Uganda's general Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 (Cap. 97, commenced 3 May 2019) plus Data Protection and Privacy Regulations 2021, covering all personal data including payment data. The National Payment Systems Act 2020 (fetched full text via ULII mirror, as the parliament.ug PDF is an OCR-garbled scan) contains payment-specific data provisions beyond general DPA coverage: s.63 (retention of payment system information), s.64 (protection of customer information - confidentiality/non-disclosure duty on licensees and the central bank), and s.65 (consumer protection in payment systems, requiring central bank rules guided by principles including data protection and confidentiality). This combination of a general data protection act plus sector-specific confidentiality/retention/consumer-protection provisions in payment legislation supports the top code on this scale (Specific Payment Data Provisions). revised_comments: Uganda's data protection framework covering payment transaction data combines the general Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 (Cap. 97), which applies to all personal data collection, processing and disclosure, with specific provisions in the National Payment Systems Act 2020. The latter includes section 63 on retention of payment system information, section 64 requiring licensees and the central bank to protect the privacy of participant and customer information and restrict its disclosure, and section 65 requiring the central bank's consumer protection rules to be guided by data protection and confidentiality principles. The Data Protection and Privacy Regulations 2021 further operationalise the general Act. Together these constitute specific payment data provisions rather than reliance on general data protection legislation alone.
